faults.note: 16^(3/4) = (⁴√16)³ = 2³ = 8 (8⁴ = 4096 = 16³); the exponent was used as a multiplier. A fractional power is outside the grammar, so the relation is named, not decided (the code table lists it under ST-PARSE-001, the grammar's Unsupported list under ST-UNDEC-001). The arithmetic 16 × 3/4 = 12 holds as written. [computed: (16 × 3/4)⁴ = 20736, 16³ = 4096: 12 is not 16^(3/4); 8⁴ = 4096 = 16³, so 16^(3/4) = 8]
